Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
247 AM PST Thu Nov 19 2026

.SYNOPSIS...19/232 AM.

Rain today, heaviest in the morning. It will bring the potential 
for flooding and wind related issues. Very large surf and high 
tides will continue, with ongoing surf and flooding hazards at the
coast. Cool and dry on Friday and Saturday. A chance of light 
rain on Sunday.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-SAT)...19/232 AM.

Today's front assoc with a 543 dam upper low over western OR is
moving slowly through the Central Coast. Prefrontal rain has
spread into VTA county and will reach LA county by 400 am. 

The front is very dynamic and has been a very efficient rain
producer with rainfall rates over an inch an hour and half hour
rates near three quarters of an inch per hour. These rates have
prompted the issuance of multiple flash flood warnings.

The upper level steering winds are now more aligned parallel to
the front and this has slowed its progress. Revised frontal
passage timing now calls for for a 600 am time for the city of
SBA; 7am to 10am for VTA county and 900 am to noon for LA county.

The front is holding together well and rainfall rates at or
exceeding 1 inch per hour are likely with the front. Rain totals
for the csts and foothills will be 1 to 3 inches with 2 to 5
inches across the coastal slopes.

These rainfall rates will very likely produce some flooding issues
across the rest of the forecast area as the front advances through
the area. Flood watches are in effect for all areas save for the
Antelope Vly.

While no lightning has been observed with the system so far, there
still is a 20 percent chc of a TSTM with the front. The impressive
rainfall rates with the front are likely assoc with low level
convection that is just not vertically developed enough to produce
lightning. Along with that, there is a very small chance, 5% or 
less, of a weak tornado with the best chances of that in the LA 
Basin later this morning.

The sfc low is fairly wound up and there is a good deal of upper
level support for advisory level southerly winds 35 to 50 mph

Freezing levels will remain above 7500 feet for all but the last
few hours of the storm, during which 3-6 inches could fall mostly
above 7000 feet. Due to the very high elevation and limited
impacts no snow related products are in effect.

Highs today will only reach the mid 60s.

Some Post frontal showers area likely, but it should be dry by the
evening.

Dry fast moving NW flow will set up over the area on Friday. It
will be a blustery and cool fall day with highs only in the lower
to mid 60s.

A little pop up ridge will move over the state on Saturday. It
will be sunny day. Max temps, however, will only rise a degree or
2 and max temps will end up 4 to 8 degrees blo normal.

.LONG TERM (SUN-WED)...19/232 AM.

A little ripple in the flow will bring a 20 to 30 percent chc of
rain to the area on Sunday. Mdls have been trending less and less
with this system. Rainfall amounts, if any, will be less than 2
tenths of an inch. Max temps will continue in the mid 60s.

A weak ridge will cross the area Monday. Dry and mostly sunny 
conditions will prevail. Temps will not change much and will
remain in the mid 60s or 4 to 8 degrees blo normal.

Better ridging and weak offshore flow will occur Tuesday morning 
Not enough offshore flow to produce any winds, but enough to bring
a little warming. Look for 2 to 3 degrees of warming and max 
temps in the mid to upper 60s. There is a slight chc that the next
storm could arrive early enough to bring some late afternoon rain
to the SLO county coast.

Still not much mdl agreement for the Tuesday night Wednesday time
period. The Central Coast will likely see some rain during this
time with only a 30-40 percent chc south of Pt Conception. This
looks like a system that can produce, at most, a half inch of
rain.

Thanksgiving, at this time, looks dry.

&&

.AVIATION...19/1032Z.

At 0832Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Low confidence in all TAFs as a cold front will move across the
forecast area. During frontal passage cig/vis will vary
frequently. MVFR conds will be most frequent but isolated IFR
conds are likely as well.  There is a 20% chance of thunderstorms
through 20/21Z.

KLAX...Low confidence in TAF. There will be frequent cig/vis
changes from 14Z-20Z. The lowest mostly likely cigs will be
BKN008. There is a 20 percent chc of a TSTM 14Z-20Z. There is a 
40 percent chance of an 8-10 kt east wind component from 
19/11Z-17Z.

KBUR...Low confidence in TAF. There will be frequent cig/vis
changes from 14Z-20Z. The lowest mostly likely cigs will be
BKN008. There is a 20 percent chc of a TSTM 14Z-20Z.

&&

.MARINE...19/246 AM.

High confidence in dangerous ocean conditions through Friday due 
to a combination of gusty winds and large seas. Gale force winds
are likely north of Pt Sal and localized gale force winds are 
possible elsewhere. Also, light to moderate rain with pockets of 
heavy rainfall is likely through the morning. This front will 
continue to progress to the southeast this morning. A marine 
weather statement (MWSLOX) has been issued to highlight the 
potential for thunderstorms. Refer to the product for more 
information. Winds will shift to the NW behind the front and 
showers will likely linger into Friday.

Seas will continue to increase due to the combination of a large 
northwest swell and southwest wind swell. Large breaking waves may
impact Morro Bay Harbor and to a lesser extent Ventura Harbor 
today through Thursday. Additionally, Pismo and Cayucos may see 
breaking waves at or over the base of the piers.

Conditions will improve through the day Friday and become relatively
mild through Saturday. A weak front will likely move through the
coastal waters Sunday into Monday but impacts look minimal at most.
Better signal for an impactful storm system around Thanksgiving 
but details are blurry at this time.

&&

.BEACHES...18/652 PM.

Dangerous conditions at the beaches will continue into Friday, 
peaking Thursday.

Large surf will create very dangerous rip currents and jetty
conditions. Additionally, minor to moderate coastal flooding 
issues may occur, especially on Thursday during peak morning 
high tide. Some impacts may be shallow seawater flooding over 
low lying beaches/walkways/parking lots and significant beach 
erosion. Impacts along the Central Coast will likely be higher 
such as localized wave damage (especially to piers, localized 
coastal flooding impacting roads and possibly structures, as 
well as breaking waves at Morro Bay Harbor.

High Surf Advisories have been issued for all beach areas. A 
Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect for the Central Coast for 
Thursday.

Extremely high tides, likely record breaking, will occur over
Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day). 
Additional swells are becoming increasingly likely next week as
well. These swells may produce period of elevated to high surf.
The combination of very high tides and increasing surf will likely
lead to at least widespread moderate-level coastal flooding 
issues across all coasts. There is potential for significant 
coastal flooding impacts if a larger swell overlaps with the
timing of the extreme tides
